messages:
mila: heads up, saw a flake where a kvcache reader issued a DMA to a stale host PA right after an async unbind. repro in nightly host-fallback. anyone seen similar?

devin: saw one trace yesterday. log looked like: 
[evict] unbind_vram page=0xabc
[mmu] notifier queued unmap pfn=0x123
[kvcache] read pfn=0x123 (stale)

sam: that ordering implies unbind published before mmu notifier completed and reader didn't see quiesce. two levers: slow the writer (wait for notifier) or make readers detect transient mapping changes.

anya: we tried writer-wait earlier but it added ~1ms on eviction tail in perf runs. can't do that on hot paths. prefer a reader-side defense.

mila: what's a light-weight reader guard? micro epoch? gen flip? sticky token?

devin: micro-epoch is simplest: bump epoch before/after remap/unbind. readers sample pre/post and if mismatch take slowpath. slowpath spins a short window then waits for notifier ack.

sam: prototype numbers: fastpath cost ~2 loads + barriers (~50ns), slowpath rare but costs ~2-200us depending on wait strategy.

anya: we should also add a CI injector to force mmu callback delays (NOTIFIER_STALL_MS) and a unit that asserts kvcache never returns mapping when mapping_valid==false.

devin: agree. telemetry: per-tenant histogram for epoch_retries and a counter for stale-mapping-drops. if retries spike we alert.

mila: edge case: two writers remapping same page quickly. make epoch 64-bit and use atomic inc to avoid races/wrap.

sam: slowpath policy suggestion: spin for up to 50us, then escalate to waiting on notifier. makes common cases cheap and bounds latency.

anya: add a feature flag so we can roll out in stages and measure retry rate on beta clusters. also add a perf microbench to validate fastpath <100ns.

devin: i'll sketch PR: DRAFT: kvcache-mapping-epoch + notifier-injector. will include tests and perf harness.

mila: quick checklist for RFC follow-up: 1) short-term epoch guard + CI injector + telemetry, 2) perf microbench and tail-latency run, 3) if retries unacceptable, propose writer-quiesce invariant (unbind waits for mmu quiesce) with migration plan.

sam: filing the draft PR now. tagging @anya for telemetry and @devin for tests.

evict-bot: CI: host-fallback (gpu-32g) flaked 2/60 runs last 24h  category=memory-ordering-race. https://ci.redwood.internal/4567

mila: thanks everyone. will add note to mem-mgmt RFC and track outcomes. :thumbsup:
